messages.author: 3803273dbdab60c6
messages.subject: cluster size in mcds
parts:
I am new to distance and I am unclear what to do with cluster size. I have run several different models different ways, but I keep getting errors.

I have point count data with many of the points having 0 detections, and others with 1 or more detections.
I have on each line a size variable that indicates the number of birds detected within a certain distance.
Some points have multiple lines, and some lines have multiple detections.

e.g.,
Point 1  Distance 25 m   0 birds detected
Point 2  Distance 25 m   1 bird detected
Point 2  Distance 50 m   2 birds detected

I want to account for all of the birds detected.

I have tried setting up the data as clusters initially, then adding the cluster size as a covariate in the MCDS engine, but I get this message: ** Warning: When cluster size is a covariate, variance of the cluster size, density of individuals, and abundance estimates can only be obtained via the bootstrap. You have not specified the bootstrap variance option, so these variance estimates will not be produced. **
** Warning: When cluster size is a covariate, encounter rates are not computed. **
** Warning: The /BIAS switch is not allowed when cluster size is a covariate, and so it has been ignored. **

I have also tried setting up the data as single observations initially, then adding cluster size as a covariate in the MCDS engine, but I get this message: SIZEC is an invalid command when OBJECT=SINGLE, and so was ignored.

Can anyone tell me what I am doing wrong?

Do I need to set the data up differently?

e.g.,
Point 1  Distance 25m   0 birds detected
Point 2  Distance 25m   1 bird detected
Point 2  Distance 50 m  1 birds detected
Point 2  Distance 50 m  1 birds detected

Or is there something else I am missing?

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] cluster size in mcds
parts:
"Freetardis"

It is not clear from your question whether your birds are detected in clusters, or whether you have binned distances and detect multiple individual birds within the same distance bin.  I'll answer as if the first situation is correct.

There are a number of Distance projects that are installed on your computer when you install the Distance software.  Have a look at the project "Songbird.dst".  This is point transect data for birds detected in clusters.  That shows the way to enter such data.

messages.author: 3803273dbdab60c6
messages.subject: Re: cluster size in mcds
parts:
Thank you Eric.

I looked at the examples, and I have entered my data as clusters. In most cases 0 or 1 bird was detected at a point, though at a few points there may have been several birds. We identified the number of birds within 4 distance bins (0-25,25-50, 50-75, 75-100). So for any point I could have 0+ birds in each bin. I do not have my data set up by bins though (i.e., I don't have 4 observations per point). Instead, I have the data set up so that if 1+ birds were detected at a point, the radial distance = mid point of bin and the cluster size = no. of bird within bin. If no birds were detected at the point, there is one line for the point with no distance and no cluster size.

I was advised to enter the midpoint of the bin as the radial distance and also to enter cutpoints representing my distance bins. I was also advised to enter the survey effort as the area of the point count circle * the number of times each circle was surveyed. However, none of the datasets I looked at in the sample Distance projects are set up that way. All advice is welcome.

example data

Point 1   0 birds detected   distance NA                       covariates NA
Point 2   1 bird  detected    distance 13 (bin 0-25)       covariates listed
Point 2   2 birds detected   distance 38 (bin 25-50)     covariates listed
Point 2   1 bird detected     distance 63 (bin 50-75)     covariates listed
Point 3   1 bird detected     distance 88 (bin 75-100)   covariates listed
Point 4   0 birds detected   distance NA                       covariates NA
